J2.evidence: Arabic «والياء المقدرة منصوب الفعل» = the implied yāʾ is what the verb governs in the accusative, i.e. its object (the yāʾ of ليعبدون = 'Me', direct object of يعبد). English 'the implied yāʾ is the object of the verb' conveys exactly this meaning; it is a translation, not an added claim. No error.

J1.evidence: «منصوب الفعل» means that which the verb puts in the accusative, which here is the verb's direct object. 'The implied yāʾ is the object of the verb' is a faithful rendering of the phrase and adds nothing. The rest of the English (lām ta'līl, أن مضمرة, حذف النون, نون الوقاية) is accurate.
